title: Build relationships inside platforms you depend on
why: Platform support inboxes often fail. Find a human inside the platform early and spread relationships so a reassignment does not cut you off.

title: Why dark themes strain some eyes: optics explained
why: Pupil dilation and lens accommodation explain how focus and depth of field shift with bright pixels on dark backgrounds, affecting readability.

title: Personal IDE preference complaints
why: Anecdotal frustration with VSCode plugins and a preference for JetBrains tools; no transferable technical lesson.

title: Proposal to bid for H1B visas by salary
why: Political policy opinion about immigration rules without substantive technical or factual content.

title: Server relief: cheap server-side password verification
why: Store SHA256 of the scrypt hash so clients pay the scrypt cost while the server verifies cheaply; a stolen database is useless for login.

title: Why Alameda's insolvency is unlikely: balance sheet logic
why: Insolvency needs a realized loss. Liabilities mirror the illiquid tokens held as assets, so a token collapse largely nets out.

title: Complaints about Python dependency tooling
why: A list of frustrations and wishes about virtualenvs and lock files, with little explanation of how the problems actually work.

title: Opinion on remote work at Yahoo
why: Personal preference and anecdotes about remote work and office schedules, without a transferable lesson.

title: Defending achievement-focused parenting
why: Personal opinion on parenting styles anchored on one autobiography; argumentative rather than informative.

title: Promoting Nano over Bitcoin
why: Promotional argument for a cryptocurrency with an article link; the claims are opinion rather than a technical explanation.

title: Why conversational writing is not transcribed speech
why: Real speech is messy and listeners edit it on the fly. Conversational prose is an idealised, edited version that takes skill to write well.

title: A teenager worries about keeping up with tech
why: Personal anxiety about a fast-moving field with no concrete lesson or technical explanation.

title: Why the Google+ names policy poisoned unified accounts
why: Unified login was reasonable, but sharing the social network's name and strict name rules made the account system politically toxic.

title: Competitor's view on GCE trust problem
why: Market opinion from an industry rival about trust and pricing; argumentative rather than a technical lesson.

title: Insider defends Facebook's integrity work
why: Unverifiable first-hand reassurance and opinion about company priorities; no concrete technical or factual lesson.

title: Arguing Amazon's free-app promotion was valuable
why: Opinion about marketing value built on sales figures; mainly argumentative rather than explanatory.

title: How Israeli airport security screens passengers, not bags
why: Screeners probe story consistency through layered conversations, trading time and profiling for depth, unlike US bag-focused screening.

title: Opinion on young unemployed peers
why: Moralizing opinion about personal responsibility and locus of control; no concrete lesson or evidence.

title: Moderator note on repeated threads
why: Moderation note about flagging and repetition on a specific topic, which is administrative rather than informative.

title: Reporter's experience reporting a state website flaw
why: Personal grievance about an agency's reaction to a disclosure; the lesson is mostly about blame, not technical knowledge.

title: Argument that remote work frees time
why: Personal opinion about office socializing and commuting time, not supported by evidence or a transferable technique.

title: Anecdote against union job classifications
why: Anecdote and opinion about unions and workplace culture, presented as a verdict rather than an explained mechanism.

title: Commentary on a crypto founder's conduct
why: Personal condemnation of a founder and political views on government; argumentative without technical content.

title: AlphaFold is homology modeling, not folding physics
why: AlphaFold matches sequences to known structures, roughly twice as accurate as older methods, but reveals little about how proteins fold or predict novel folds.

title: Proposal for a tech company ombudsman
why: A policy proposal for a paid escalation channel; an opinion about company support, not a technical explanation.

title: Cloud vendors profit from open source
why: Opinion about licensing and cloud economics with no explanation beyond general claims about incentives.

title: Personal theft story and police inaction
why: Personal grievance and call for crowdsourced video posting; anecdotal with no transferable lesson for technical readers.

title: CPAP device phones home undisclosed
why: Personal anecdote about undisclosed data collection; a concern rather than a technical explanation of how it works.

title: CEO responds to student complaints
why: Corporate response defending a school's resourcing and management; a PR statement rather than explanatory knowledge.

title: Why distro patches frustrate upstream maintainers
why: Distributions patch and reallocate interfaces without asking, so maintainers lose control of their own interface and inherit user bugs they never introduced.

title: Opinions comparing performance languages
why: Subjective ratings of languages for dev time and performance with no measurements; mainly opinion invites debate.

title: Sales fundamentals from a veteran sales leader
why: Sell aspirin, not vitamins. People buy time, money, sex, or peace of mind, and being useful builds the trust that drives sales.

title: Defending QR code menus
why: Personal experience and preference about restaurant ordering, mostly persuasive rather than explanatory.

title: Commentary on class and tech culture
why: Personal reflection and criticism of commenters about class and mindset; a social opinion rather than a technical lesson.

title: Science's exponential growth era has ended
why: Goodstein argues science's institutions were built for exponential expansion and are unsuited to the steady-state era that followed, so expectations must change.

title: Reflection on free time and productivity
why: Personal reflection on career breaks and procrastination; relatable but with no concrete, transferable insight.

title: Argument that college is worth finishing
why: Opinion about persistence and degrees, supported by an anecdote about a friend rather than evidence.

title: Maintaining Python across Google's monorepo
why: Google upgraded Python from 2.7 to 3.11 over years, since committers own breakages, while tooling kept thousands of third-party packages patched and current.

title: Alan Kay's frame: most real-world code is pop culture
why: Pop culture is identity-driven and present-focused, which explains why new, hip solutions often beat proven ones in industry decisions.

title: Media multitasking studies do not cover listening to music
why: The cited MMI measure covers concurrent screen media like email and Netflix, so it does not show that background music harms focus.

title: Practical lessons from leaving Google services
why: Migrating accounts takes a day; many sites block custom domains or keep old logins, so use aliases and CCPA deletion requests for less trusted sites.

title: Why ignoring database internals causes data loss
why: Treating databases as black boxes led to missing transactions, MongoDB async buffering data loss, and projects with missing or wrong indexes.

title: Docker creator responds to Rocket announcement
why: A reply mainly defending Docker against a rival's press campaign; the design principles are context-bound to the dispute.

title: Critique of a tech founder's open letter
why: Personal critique of a letter's tone and grand claims about education; opinion rather than explanation.

title: Proof-of-work energy scales with market cap
why: Mining arbitrage ties electricity spent to Bitcoin's market value, so energy use grows with price until it becomes unsustainable, a clear mental model.

title: Raft is MultiPaxos, not a rival consensus algorithm
why: Paxos is a family of ideas, and standard Paxos decides one value. Raft is a concrete specification of MultiPaxos ideas, so comparing them is misleading.

title: Argument that code reading matters more
why: A thesis about literacy and reading code that is mostly opinion, with a link to the author's own approach rather than evidence.

title: Refund fight over a lost expensive order
why: A consumer complaint about escalation delays; the useful advice is cut off and mostly anecdotal.

title: Developers want greenfield over maintenance
why: Opinion and anecdote about developer career incentives and rewrite urges, without a concrete method or evidence.

title: Critique of Apple's 2016 MacBook decisions
why: Opinionated critique of Apple's hardware choices with speculation about motives; argumentative rather than explanatory.

title: Why Apple's M1 is fast: width and balance
why: M1 speed comes from very wide decode, a 630-entry reorder buffer, large caches and high memory bandwidth, balanced to keep power low.

title: Argument that cryptocurrency is gambling
why: Strong opinion about crypto's worth and externalities; some mining figures but framed as argument rather than explanation.

title: Why Ruby is a poor first language
why: Opinion on language choice with a few language-design points, mainly arguing against a book rather than teaching a concept.

title: Long-term Airbnb renter's complaints
why: Personal grievances about host quality, support and burglary; anecdotal with no transferable technical lesson.

title: Wishlist for Python packaging
why: A list of pet peeves and wishes about setup files and virtualenvs; reasonable preferences rather than explained knowledge.

title: Go versus Rust: building versus maintaining
why: Opinion about language longevity and hype cycles; an argumentative prediction rather than a verifiable explanation.

title: Nostalgia for mastering old video games
why: Personal nostalgia about childhood gaming and self-set challenges; no concrete lesson.

title: Intermittent outage traced to warehouse activity
why: Checking physical causes helps: an intermittent network fault correlated with pallet removals, found by observing the environment, not the logs.

title: Building Naughty Dog's games in a Lisp dialect
why: The author wrote GOOL and GOAL, Lisp-based runtime dialects that shipped Crash Bandicoot and Jak and Daxter, before Ruby replaced Lisp for libraries.

title: Dark matter is an inconsistency, not a discovered substance
why: Dark matter and dark energy name mismatches between predicted and observed motion. The names imply a known substance, when the real finding is a gap in theory.

title: Rebuttal to Paul Graham on evolution
why: A debate reply that mostly rebuts a strawman and argues over fallacies; the lasting content is argument rather than knowledge.

title: Anonymous account of a bad manager
why: Personal anecdote about abusive management and overtime; a grievance rather than a transferable technical lesson.

title: Ambition: fixing poor countries versus Mars
why: Philosophical opinion about ambition and values, with no concrete knowledge or method to learn.

title: Judge's advice on indie game sales
why: Opinion that success requires cheating with fake reviews; a cynical claim without evidence, offered as advice.

title: Why educational games struggle to sell
why: Institutional buyers pick boring features, while parents do not spread word of mouth for narrow age ranges, so media companies win on cheap exposure.

title: Developers should learn rebase and cherry-pick
why: A plea about git habits with a personal anecdote; advice is generic and the detail is limited to tool recommendations.

title: Argument against government-backed college loans
why: Political opinion about loans and degree value; argumentative with no cited data on costs.

title: Personal account of a Danish birth
why: A personal, positive account of midwife-led childbirth; warm but without a technical or explanatory lesson for a curious reader.

title: Startup tech stack advice
why: Opinionated advice to use Rails then Scala for scale, with a lot of personal preference and little supporting evidence.

title: Why huge neural nets generalize: depth-to-width ratio
why: Per the book's epilogue, generalization of very large networks depends on the depth-to-width ratio, which controls data-dependent couplings between neurons.

title: Four conversation books converge on the same elements
why: Difficult Conversations, NVC, Crucial Conversations and Getting Past No share core steps; NVC's edge is concrete recipes, while the others explain why.

title: Teevox shutdown and a PG quote
why: Personal memories of a failed startup and a quote about rushing to judgment; a story rather than a transferable lesson.

title: How Minimoog-style synth controls map to organ pipes
why: Footage labels like 16' and 8' are organ pipe lengths giving octaves. LO is a subsonic setting used for modulation on real synths.

title: Personal case for using Bitcoin to get paid
why: Personal argument for Bitcoin in countries with kleptocracy; opinion-based and mixed with contested claims about the internet.

title: Personal reflection on calling parents
why: A personal reflection on family contact and parenthood; moving but with no concrete lesson for technical readers.

title: NeWS synchronous events versus X11 input focus
why: NeWS blocked event distribution until synchronous handlers ran, avoiding focus errors. Asynchronous X11 clients cannot do this, so their focus tracking is flaky.

title: A developer's list of personal gear
why: A list of personal tools and hardware with product links and brief opinions; no explanatory content.

title: Defending copyright protection in software
why: Long argument about copyright policy and abuses; a values-based opinion rather than an explanation of the case's technical facts.

title: Structuring web apps around the database as an OS
why: Three-tier apps layer ad-hoc RPC over HTTP and access control on top of the database. A database-OS approach proposes collapsing those layers.

title: Why lead toxicity varies: metallothionein production
why: Metallothionein proteins bind metals for use or removal. Genetic predisposition and environment explain why only some exposed people show symptoms.

title: Argument over whether taxation is extortion
why: A heated exchange about taxation and rights that turns into argument rather than knowledge.

title: Joke about a Scientology deposition
why: A joke-laden anecdote about an in-joke and a deposition; entertaining but with no technical or explanatory lesson.

title: Schmidt and Hunter's meta-analysis of hiring methods
why: A 1998 meta-analysis finds most hiring methods weakly predictive, with only two procedures working reasonably well at a validity near 0.5.

title: Reading SBCL's inferred function type declarations
why: SBCL infers function types such as FUNCTION with VALUES and uses static analysis for optimization, delegating checks to runtime where types overlap.

title: Paul Graham's 2010 predictions: innovation, biotech, metrics
why: Empires fall when people cannot make money building things. Metrics shape behaviour, since you make what you measure, and efficient markets spread via information.

title: Argument that Facebook's bans make it dull
why: Opinion about media framing and platform bans, arguing about labels such as fringe rather than explaining a mechanism.

title: Why early multi-touch was technically hard
why: Touch systems had to map a finger's amorphous contact blob to one intended pixel and track several fingers at once, which was not previously solved.

title: Why voluntary response polls cannot support inferences
why: Self-selected respondents are not a random sample, so voluntary response results cannot generalize to the population however large the sample.

title: Why perceptual hashes are weaker than cryptographic hashes
why: Cryptographic hashes resist collisions, but perceptual hashes match similar content by design, making them easier to attack; Apple's second hash cannot be verified.

title: Insider history of Guile at Cygnus
why: The author recounts earlier failed Scheme extension attempts and how Cygnus's free-software strategy shaped the project.

title: Moderator advice on commenting in a commons
why: A moderator's guidance on behaviour and community norms; valuable for the forum but not a technical explanation.

title: Negative review of a Chomsky book
why: A reposted partisan review that argues against Chomsky's political writing; opinion-driven rather than explanatory.

title: Rant about stagnant desktop displays
why: A rant about displays and the PC industry; opinionated complaints without a concrete technical explanation.

title: Uber CEO layoff email
why: A corporate announcement of job cuts; a company statement rather than explanatory knowledge.

title: Why real systems value evolvable schemas over type elegance
why: The hard part of engineering is changing deployed code. Protobuf's evolution rules matter more than type-theoretic elegance, which does not guarantee safe change.

title: Career advice on ownership and code review
why: Mixed career advice and a personal grievance about penalized refactoring; the practical points are generic.

title: Pro user complains about USB removal
why: A venting complaint about dongles and port removal; emotional and opinion-based without a technical explanation.

title: How a record gigapixel London panorama was shot
why: Four synchronized cameras on precision robots, 128GB cards, and laptops for copying; shooting took three days after two days of setup.

title: Why security.txt drew automated low-quality reports
why: A maintainer found a standard disclosure channel attracted automated scanner reports and wasted time, so published contacts invite high volume.

title: Porting Metal Gear Solid to PC in 1999
why: Textures covered body parts, allowing 16-colour palettes; music fit a 512KB ADPCM buffer; the executable swapped overlays around a shared 600KB core.
